titleEn: The Glory of Kings — The Line of Shem, Makeda’s Welcome, and the Gifts to Her Son (ch. 83–86)
part: ch. 83–86 — The Line of Shem, Makeda’s Welcome, and the Gifts to Her Son
about: Chapter 83 lists the kings descended from Ishmael and from Isaac, all of Shem’s line, and ends on Christ as king of kings. In chapter 84 the king of Ethiopia returns home in joy; Makeda is told by messengers, summons her people, and the Ark is brought to her city. In 85 she sees Zion and worships, tents are pitched at Däbrä Makeda, guards are set over the Ark, and the realms of Solomon and Makeda are praised. In 86 she crowns her son and gives him horses, mules, gold and the regalia.

sentences.t: ፹፫ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ እስማኤላውያን ።
sentences.l: 83. Concerning king-of Ishmaelites
sentences.i: Chapter 83: Concerning the King of the Ishmaelites
sentences.n: Chapter heading. በእንተ ‘concerning’ takes the construct: ንጉሠ is ንጉሥ ‘king’ in construct, ‘king of’. እስማኤላውያን ‘Ishmaelites’ is the adjective እስማኤላዊ (the name እስማኤል with -ዊ) in the plural -ውያን (‘those of Ishmael’), the ending that marks peoples. The number ፹፫ is 83. The chapter, in fact, speaks of kings in the plural.

sentences.t: ወበእንተዝ ፡ ኮኑ ፡ ነገሥተ ፡ ደቂቀ ፡ ይስማዔል ፡ ላዕለ ፡ ትርብ ፡ ወላዕለ ፡ ቅብጥ ፡ ወላዕለ ፡ ኖባ ፡ ወሶበ ፡ ወኵርጒ ፡ ወሪፊ ፡ ወማካ ፡ ወሞርና ፡ ወፊንቃና ፡ ወኣርሲባና ፡ ወሊባ ፡ ወመስዕ ፤
sentences.l: And-on-account-of-this became kings-of sons-of Ishmael over Tarb and-over Copts and-over Nuba and-Sobo and-Kurgu and-Rifi and-Maka and-Morna and-Finqana and-Arsibana and-Liba and-Mesʿ ;
sentences.i: And on this account the sons of Ishmael became kings over Tarb (?), over the Copts, over Nubia, and Sobo, Kurgu, Rifi, Maka, Morna, Finqana, Arsibana, Liba, and Mesʿ (?; the names after Nubia are unidentified);
sentences.n: ወበእንተዝ ‘and on account of this’ (በእንተ + ዝ). ኮኑ ‘they became’ (perfect 3mp of ኮነ); ነገሥተ ደቂቀ ይስማዔል is literally ‘kings-of sons-of Ishmael’; I read it as a predicate with the sons of Ishmael as subject, ‘the sons of Ishmael became kings’ (the -ä endings can be accusative or construct, so the chain is uncertain, ?). ላዕለ ‘over’ is repeated with ወ- for the first three names (ትርብ, ቅብጥ, ኖባ); the later names ride on it. The list is a catalogue of peoples and lands, mostly of Africa (Arabia too, ?): ቅብጥ is the Copts (Egypt), ኖባ Nubia, ሊባ perhaps Libya; ትርብ, ሶበ, ኵርጒ, ሪፊ, ማካ, ሞርና, ፊንቃና, ኣርሲባና and መስዕ I cannot identify with confidence, and I give them in transliteration (?). The Ishmaelites hold power because Ishmael, too, is of the line of Shem (next unit).

sentences.t: እስመ ፡ ዘርአ ፡ ሴም ፡ ውእቱ ።
sentences.l: For seed-of Shem he.
sentences.i: For he is of the seed of Shem.
sentences.n: እስመ ‘for’ introduces the reason. ዘርአ ‘seed of’ is construct; ሴም is Shem, son of Noah (Genesis 10:21–31; 11:10–26 carries the line down to Abraham), whose line includes Abraham and so both Ishmael and Isaac. ውእቱ ‘he’ is the copula.

sentences.t: ወዘርአ ፡ ይስሓቅኒ ፡ ነግሠ ፡ ላዕለ ፡ ይሁዳ ፡ ወላዕለ ፡ አሞሬዎን ፡ ወላዕለ ፡ ኬጤዎን ፡ ወኢያቡሴዎን ፡ ወፌርዜዎን ፡ ወኤዌዎን ፡ ወኬልቄዴዎን ፡ ወሮምያ ፡ ወአንጾክያ ፡ ወሶርያ ፡ ወአርማንያ ፡ ወፍልስጥኤም ፡ ወኢትዮጵያ ፡ ወኤዶም ፡ ወኢሎፍሊ ፡ ወኢዮኣብ ፡ ወዓማሌቅ ፡ ወአፍራግያ ፡ ወባቢሎን ፡ ወዮናንስጥ ፡ ወዕብራይስጥ ።
sentences.l: And-seed-of Isaac-also reigned over Judah and-over Amorites and-over Hittites and-Jebusites and-Perizzites and-Hivites and-Kelkedeans and-Rome and-Antioch and-Syria and-Armenia and-Philistia and-Ethiopia and-Edom and-Ilofli and-Ioab and-Amalek and-Afragya and-Babylon and-Yonanst and-Hebrew.
sentences.i: And the seed of Isaac also reigned over Judah, over the Amorites, the Hittites, the Jebusites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, the Kelkedeans (?), Rome, Antioch, Syria, Armenia, Philistia, Ethiopia, Edom, the Ilofli (the “Foreigners”, i.e. Philistines, as elsewhere in this book), Ioab (?), Amalek, Afragya (?), Babylon, Yonanst (?), and the Hebrews (?).
sentences.n: ወዘርአ ይስሓቅኒ: the enclitic -ኒ adds ‘also, indeed’ and sets Isaac’s seed beside Ishmael’s. ነግሠ ‘he reigned’ is singular, agreeing with the collective ዘርአ. The first names are the Canaanite peoples of Exodus 3:8, compare Genesis 15:19–21 (አሞሬዎን Amorites, ኬጤዎን Hittites, ኢያቡሴዎን Jebusites, ፌርዜዎን Perizzites, ኤዌዎን Hivites). Then come Rome and Antioch, Syria and Armenia, Philistia, Ethiopia, Edom, Amalek and Babylon. ኬልቄዴዎን may be Chaldeans or Chalcedon; ኢሎፍሊ is, as in chs. 49–81, ‘foreigners, Philistines’ (Greek allophyloi, Psalm 87:4); of the rest, ኢዮኣብ (Moab?), አፍራግያ (Africa or Phrygia?), ዮናንስጥ (Greece or the Greeks?) and ዕብራይስጥ (the Hebrews or their language?) are uncertain (?). The book wants the line of Isaac to hold the Christian world, the Ethiopian kingdom included.

sentences.t: እስመ ፡ ኵላ ፡ መንግሥት ፡ በከመ ፡ መሐለ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ወሀቦሙ ፡ ለዘርአ ፡ ሴም ፤
sentences.l: For all kingdom as swore God and-gave-them to-seed-of Shem;
sentences.i: For God, as he had sworn, gave all kingship to them, to the seed of Shem;
sentences.n: በከመ ‘as, according as’ + መሐለ ‘he swore’ (perfect). ወሀቦሙ ‘and he gave them’ (ወ- + perfect + -ሙ ‘them’, m. pl.), and the ለ- phrase ለዘርአ ሴም names the recipients again, as in ch. 81 (ዘኮነ ለዘርአ ሴም). ኵላ መንግሥት ‘all kingship’ is the object (accusative -ä on ኵሉ).

sentences.t: ልዑል ፡ መንበር ፡ ወምኵናን ፡ ለዘርአ ፡ ሴም ፡ በከመ ፡ ባረኮ ፡ አቡሁ ፡ ኖኅ ፡ በቃለ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ለሤም ፡ ወልዲ ፡ እንዘ ፡ ይብል ፡ ኵን ፡ እግዚአ ፡ ለአኀዊከ ፡ ወንግሥ ፡ ላዕሌሆሙ ፤
sentences.l: High throne and-authority to-seed-of Shem as blessed-him father-his Noah by-word-of God to-Shem son-his while he-says: Be lord to-your-brothers and-reign over-them;
sentences.i: The seed of Shem has the high throne and authority, as his father Noah blessed Shem, his son, by the word of God, saying: “Be lord over your brothers, and reign over them”;
sentences.n: ልዑል መንበር ‘high throne’ and ምኵናን ‘authority, rule’ carry no verb: ‘(there is) high throne … to the seed of Shem’, a nominal sentence with ለ- of possession. ባረኮ ‘he blessed him’; በቃለ ‘by the word of’ (construct). ለሤም ወልዲ ‘to Shem, his son’: ወልዲ is ወልድ with -ዲ written for the 3ms suffix -ሁ, as elsewhere in this book (‘my son’ is the other possible reading, ?). እንዘ ይብል ‘saying’ is the standard quotation frame. The imperatives ኵን ‘be!’ and ንግሥ ‘reign!’ echo Isaac’s blessing of Jacob, Genesis 27:29 (‘be lord over your brothers’); the book puts it in Noah’s mouth for Shem, whom Genesis 9:26 also blesses.

sentences.t: ወዘንተ ፡ ዘይቤ ፡ በእንተ ፡ መድኅን ፡ ዘለኵልነ ፡ ንጉሥ ፡ ኢየሱስ ፡ ክርስቶስ ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ ሰማያት ፡ ወምድር ፡ ዘውእቱ ፡ ያዐቢ ፡ ነገሥተ ፡ ወለእለ ፡ ፈቀደ ፡ ካዕበ ፡ ይስዕር ፡ ስልጣኖሙ ፤
sentences.l: And-this which he-said concerning saviour who-for-all-of-us king Jesus Christ king-of heavens and-earth, who-he he-makes-great kings and-for-those he-wished again he-abolishes authority-their;
sentences.i: And this that he said was about the Saviour, who is king for all of us, Jesus Christ, king of heaven and earth, who it is that makes kings great, and who again abolishes the authority of those he wishes to (?);
sentences.n: ዘንተ ‘this’ (accusative of the demonstrative) ዘይቤ ‘which he said’ (ዘ- + perfect). መድኅን ‘saviour’; ዘለኵልነ ‘who is for all of us’ (ዘ- + ለ- + ኵሉ + -ነ ‘us’). ንጉሠ ሰማያት ወምድር ‘king of heaven and earth’, constructs. ዘውእቱ ‘who (it is)’ + ያዐቢ ‘he makes great’, imperfect of the causative አዐበየ. The close reads ‘for those whom he wished again to abolish their authority’: ፈቀደ ‘he wished’ + ይስዕር ‘he abolishes’ (ሰዐረ ‘destroy, abolish’); the exact grammar is hard (?). The pious turn: the earthly kings listed above hold power only from Christ, the true king (compare Daniel 2:21).

sentences.t: እስመ ፡ ሎቱ ፡ ክሂል ፡ ወስልጣን ፡ ላዕለ ፡ ኵሉ ፡ ፍጥረት ፡ ለዓለመ ፡ ዓለም ፡ አሜን ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.l: For to-him power and-authority over all creation to-age-of age. Amen.
sentences.i: For to him belong power and authority over all creation, for ever and ever. Amen.
sentences.n: ሎቱ ‘to him’ (ለ- + the 3ms suffix -ቱ) with no verb: ‘to him (belong)’. ክሂል ‘power’; ስልጣን ‘authority’. ለዓለመ ዓለም ‘to the age of the age’ is the doxology formula, ‘for ever and ever’, as in Greek eis tous aionas ton aionon. The ፨ ፨ ፨ is a closing ornament of the chapter.

sentences.t: ፹፬ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ ኢትዮጵያ ፡ ዘከመ ፡ ገብአ ፡ ሀገሩ ።
sentences.l: 84. Concerning king-of Ethiopia how returned his-city
sentences.i: Chapter 84: Concerning the King of Ethiopia, How He Returned to His City
sentences.n: Chapter heading. ዘከመ ‘how, in what way’ + ገብአ ‘he returned’ (perfect 3ms). ሀገሩ ‘his city’ (ሀገር + -ሁ, with the -ሁ giving -u) is the goal, with no preposition. The number ፹፬ is 84. The king is Menelik, named David at his anointing in ch. 38–39 (see unit 17).

sentences.t: ወንጉሠ ፡ ኢትዮጵያሰ ፡ ቦአ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ሀገሩ ፡ በዐቢይ ፡ ፍሥሓ ፡ ወተድላ ፡ ምስለ ፡ ኵሉ ፡ ቃለ ፡ ማሕሌቶሙ ፡ ወዕንዚራቲሆሙ ፡ ወሰረገላቲሆሙ ፡ ከመ ፡ ኀይለ ፡ ሰማያዊያን ፡ እንዘ ፡ ይረውጹ ፡ በጽሑ ፡ ደወሎሙ ፡ እምኢየሩሳሌም ፡ በዕለት ፡ ሀገረ ፡ ወቄሮም ።
sentences.l: And-king-of Ethiopia-as-for entered into city-his in-great joy and-delight with all voice-of their-songs and-their-harps and-their-chariots like host-of heavenly-ones while they-run arrived bells-their from Jerusalem on-day-of city and-Qerom.
sentences.i: As for the king of Ethiopia, he entered his city in great joy and delight, with all the sound of their songs, their harps and their chariots, like a host of heavenly beings; as they ran, they arrived, their bells (?) coming from Jerusalem, on the day of the city and Qerom (?).
sentences.n: ንጉሠ ኢትዮጵያሰ: the enclitic -ሰ is contrastive, ‘as for’, turning from the Ishmaelites to Ethiopia. ቦአ ‘he entered’. በዐቢይ ፍሥሓ ‘in great joy’ (በ- ‘in, with’). ቃለ ‘voice of’ (construct). The nouns ማሕሌቶሙ ‘their songs’, ዕንዚራቲሆሙ ‘their harps’, ሰረገላቲሆሙ ‘their chariots’ carry -ሙ / -ሆሙ ‘their’. ከመ ኀይለ ሰማያዊያን ‘like the host of the heavenly ones’ (ሰማያዊ ‘heavenly’). እንዘ ይረውጹ ‘while they run’ (እንዘ + imperfect). ደወሎሙ I take as ‘their bells’ (?); in በዕለት ሀገረ ወቄሮም the sense ‘on the day of the city and Qerom’ is uncertain, and ቄሮም is probably a place name (?).

sentences.t: ወለአኩ ፡ ላቲ ፡ በአሕማር ፡ ከመ ፡ ይንግርዋ ፡ ለማክዳ ፡ ንግሥተ ፡ ኢትዮጵያ ፡ ወአርድእዋ ፡ ዘከመ ፡ ረከቡ ፡ ኵሎ ፡ ሠናያተ ፡ ወዘከመ ፡ ነግሠ ፡ ወልዳ ፡ ወዘከመ ፡ አምጽእዋ ፡ ለጽዮን ፡ ሰማያዊት ፡ ተዜነወት ፡ ዘንተ ፡ ኵሎ ፡ ክብረ ፡ ወአዖደት ፡ ዐዋዴ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ኵሉ ፡ መንግሥት ፡ ዘእምታሕቴሃ ፡ ከመ ፡ ትትቀበሎ ፡ ለወልዳ ፡ ወፈድፋደሰ ፡ ዘበእንተ ፡ ጽዮን ፡ ሰማያዊት ፡ ታቦተ ፡ አምላከ ፡ እስራኤል ፤
sentences.l: And-they-sent to-her by-ships that they-tell-her to-Makeda queen-of Ethiopia and-her-disciples how they-found all good-things and-how reigned her-son and-how they-brought-her to-Zion heavenly she-was-informed this all glory and-she-sent-round herald into all kingdom which-from-beneath-her that she-receive-him her-son and-especially that-concerning Zion heavenly ark-of God-of Israel;
sentences.i: And they sent to her by ships to tell Makeda, queen of Ethiopia, and her followers (?) how they had found all good things, how her son had become king, and how they had brought heavenly Zion; she was informed of all this glory, and she sent a herald (?) round through the whole kingdom beneath her, that they receive her son, and above all that which concerned heavenly Zion, the ark of the God of Israel;
sentences.n: ወለአኩ ‘and they sent’ (perfect 3mp); ላቲ ‘to her’; በአሕማር ‘by ships’ (አሕማር plural of ሐመር). ከመ ይንግርዋ ‘that they tell her’ (ከመ + subjunctive + -ዋ ‘her’). ለማክዳ ንግሥተ ኢትዮጵያ ‘Makeda, queen of Ethiopia’, queen in construct. አርድእዋ ‘her disciples’; here likely her followers or officials (?). ዘከመ ‘how’ is repeated three times, each with a perfect verb. አምጽእዋ ለጽዮን ‘they brought her, Zion’: Zion, the Ark, is grammatically feminine (cf. ‘the heavenly Zion’ ሰማያዊት). ተዜነወት ‘she was informed’ (tä-stem, 3fs). አዖደት ‘she sent round’ (causative of ዐወደ, ‘go round’) with ዐዋዴ ‘a herald or proclamation’ (?). ዘእምታሕቴሃ ‘which (is) from beneath her’, i.e. under her rule (ዘ- + እም- + ታሕት + -ሃ). ከመ ትትቀበሎ ‘that they receive him’ (ተቀበለ, 3fs for the kingdom). ወፈድፋደሰ ‘and above all’. ታቦተ ‘ark of’: Zion is the Ark of the Covenant (ታቦት), which Menelik brought from Jerusalem; this is the book’s central theology.

sentences.t: ወነፍኁ ፡ ቀርነ ፡ በቅድሜሃ ፡ ውተፈሥሑ ፡ ኵሎሙ ፡ ሰብአ ፡ ኢትዮጵያ ፡ እምንኡስ ፡ እስከ ፡ ዐቢይ ፡ ወእምተባዕት ፡ እስከ ፡ አንስት ፤
sentences.l: And-they-blew horn before-her and-rejoiced all-of-them men-of Ethiopia from-small until great and-from-male until females;
sentences.i: They blew the horn before her, and all the people of Ethiopia rejoiced, from small to great, from males to females;
sentences.n: ወነፍኁ ‘and they blew’ (perfect 3mp) with ቀርነ ‘horn’ (accusative). ውተፈሥሑ is written so in the source, an apparent slip for ወተፈሥሑ ‘and they rejoiced’ (tä-stem). ሰብአ ‘men of’, construct. እምንኡስ እስከ ዐቢይ ‘from the small to the great’ (እም- ‘from’, እስከ ‘until’), the first of the merism pairs this part loves (see unit 19).

sentences.t: ወተንሥኡ ፡ ፀብኣ ፡ ምስሌሃ ፡ ከመ ፡ ይትቀበልዎ ፡ ለንጉሦሙ ።
sentences.l: And-they-rose host with-her that they-receive-him to-their-king.
sentences.i: They rose in force (?) with her, to receive their king.
sentences.n: ተንሥኡ ‘they rose’ (perfect 3mp). ፀብኣ ‘a host, in battle array’, accusative, from ፀብእ ‘war, army’ (?). It could also be ፀብእ with the suffix -ሃ, ‘her army’ (?). ከመ ይትቀበልዎ ‘that they receive him’ (ተቀበለ, ይትቀበልዎ with -ዎ ‘him’); ለንጉሦሙ ‘their king’ marks the object with ለ-, as usual with ተቀበለ.

sentences.t: ወበጽሐት ፡ ሀገረ ፡ ምስፍና ፡ እንተ ፡ ይእቲ ፡ ርእሰ ፡ መንግሥተ ፡ ኢትዮጵያ ፡ ዘበደኃሪ ፡ መዋዕል ፡ ኮነ ፡ ርእሰ ፡ ክርስትያነ ፡ ኢትዮጵያ ፤
sentences.l: And-she-arrived city-of Məsfəna which she head-of kingdom-of Ethiopia which-in-last days became head-of Christians-of Ethiopia;
sentences.i: She arrived at the city of Məsfəna (?), which is the head of the kingdom of Ethiopia and which in later days became the head of the Christians of Ethiopia;
sentences.n: ወበጽሐት ‘and she arrived’ (3fs perfect, taking an accusative of place, ሀገረ). ምስፍና is ‘rule, lordship’ and here a place name, ‘the city of rule’ (?). እንተ ይእቲ ‘which she is’ is the feminine relative with the copula; ርእሰ ‘head of’ construct. ዘበደኃሪ መዋዕል ‘which in the latter days’, ኮነ ‘it became’. The author looks back from a Christian Ethiopia: the Queen’s old capital becomes the Christian capital.

sentences.t: ወውስቴታ ፡ አስተዳለወት ፡ ዕፍረተ ፡ ዘአልቦ ፡ ኆልቈ ፡ እምነ ፡ ህንድ ፡ ወእምነ ፡ ባልቴ ፡ እስከ ፡ ጋልቴት ፡ ወእምነ ፡ አልሳፉ ፡ እስከ ፡ አዘዘት ፡ ወአስተጋብአት ።
sentences.l: And-in-it she-prepared perfume which-not-with-it number from India and-from Balte until Galtet and-from Alsafu until Azazet and-she-gathered.
sentences.i: There she prepared perfumes without number, from India, from Balte to Galtet, and from Alsafu to Azazet (the four names are unknown, ?), and she gathered them.
sentences.n: ውስቴታ ‘in it’ (ውስተ + -ታ), the city. አስተዳለወት ‘she prepared’ (a quadriliteral causative). ዕፍረተ ‘perfume’ (accusative); ዘአልቦ ኆልቈ ‘that has no number’ (ዘ- + አልቦ ‘there is not’ + ኆልቈ ‘number’). ህንድ is India. ባልቴ, ጋልቴት, አልሳፉ and አዘዘት are not known to me and are given in transliteration (?). አስተጋብአት ‘she gathered’ (causative-reflexive stem), with no object stated.

sentences.t: ወመጽአ ፡ ወልዳ ፡ እንተ ፡ ፍኖተ ፡ አዝያባ ፡ ወቂሮ ፡ ወወፅአ ፡ እንተ ፡ መሰስ ፡ ወዐርገ ፡ ቡር ፡ ወመጽአ ፡ ሀገረ ፡ ምስፍና ፡ ርእሰ ፡ ኢትዮጵያ ፡ ዘለሊሃ ፡ አሕነጸታ ፡ በስማ ፡ ወተብህለት ፡ ደብረ ፡ ማክዳ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.l: And-came her-son by way-of Azyaba and-Qiro and-went-out by Mäsäs and-went-up Bur and-came city-of Məsfəna head-of Ethiopia which she-herself she-built-it in-her-name and-it-was-called Mount-of Makeda.
sentences.i: Her son came by the road of Azyaba and Qiro (?), went out by Mäsäs (?), went up to Bur (?), and came to the city of Məsfəna, the head of Ethiopia, which she herself had built and named after herself, and it was called Däbrä Makeda, the Mount of Makeda.
sentences.n: ወመጽአ ‘and he came’; ወልዳ ‘her son’ (ወልድ + -ሃ) is Menelik, now David. እንተ ፍኖተ I read as ‘by the road of’ (?); the feminine relative እንተ is used as a preposition. ወወፅአ ‘went out’, ወዐርገ ‘went up’ (ዐርገ ‘ascend’), with the places መሰስ and ቡር (?). ዘለሊሃ አሕነጸታ ‘which she herself built it’ (አሕነጸት, 3fs perfect of the causative አሕነጸ of ሐነጸ ‘build’, + -ኣ ‘it’, giving -ታ; ለሊሃ ‘herself’). በስማ ‘in her name’. ተብህለት ‘it was called’ (tä-stem of ብህለ, 3fs). ደብረ ‘mount of’ construct. The series of ፨ marks the chapter’s end.

sentences.t: ፹፭ ፡ ኀበ ፡ ተፈሥሐት ፡ ማክዳ ፡ ንግሥት ።
sentences.l: 85. Where rejoiced Makeda queen
sentences.i: Chapter 85: Where Queen Makeda Rejoiced
sentences.n: Chapter heading. ኀበ ‘where, in the place in which’ is a relative conjunction here, ‘(the place) where she rejoiced’; ተፈሥሐት is the tä-stem perfect of ፈሥሐ ‘rejoice’, 3fs. The number ፹፭ is 85. Note the spelling ማክዳ here and መክዳ later in this part.

sentences.t: ወበጽሐ ፡ ዳዊት ፡ ንጉሥ ፡ በዐቢይ ፡ ግርማ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ሀገረ ፡ እሙ ፤
sentences.l: And-arrived David king in-great majesty into city-of his-mother;
sentences.i: King David arrived with great majesty at the city of his mother;
sentences.n: ወበጽሐ ‘and he arrived’ (3ms). ዳዊት ንጉሥ ‘King David’ is Menelik, who took the name David at his anointing in Jerusalem (ch. 38–39). ግርማ ‘majesty, awe’. ሀገረ እሙ ‘the city of his mother’ (እም + -ሁ, written እሙ).

sentences.t: ወእምዝ ፡ ርእየታ ፡ በመልዕልት ፡ ለጽዮን ፡ ቅድስት ፡ እንዘ ፡ ታበርህ ፡ ከመ ፡ እንተ ፡ ፀሐይ ፡ ወሶበ ፡ ርእየታ ፡ አእኰተቶ ፡ ወሰብሐቶ ፡ ለአምላከ ፡ እስራኤል ፡ ወሰገደት ፡ ወጐድአት ፡ እንግድዓሃ ፡ ወአልዐለት ፡ ርእሳ ፡ ወነጸረት ፡ ውስተ ፡ ሰማያት ፡ ወአእኰተቶ ፡ ለፈጣሪሃ ፡ ወጠፍሐት ፡ በእደዊሃ ፡ ወየበበት ፡ በአፉሃ ፡ ወአጽሐሰት ፡ በእገሪሃ ፡ ወአሰርገወት ፡ ኵሎ ፡ ሥጋሃ ፡ በፍሥሓ ፡ ወተሐሥየት ፡ በመንፈስ ፡ ኵሉ ፡ ውሳጥያቲሃ ።
sentences.l: And-then she-saw-her in-the-height Zion holy while she-shines like that-of sun and-when she-saw-her she-gave-thanks-to-him and-she-praised-him God-of Israel and-she-bowed and-she-bent her-neck and-she-lifted her-head and-she-gazed into heavens and-she-gave-thanks-to-him to-her-Creator and-she-spread with-her-hands and-she-cried with-her-mouth and-she-trod with-her-feet and-she-adorned all her-flesh in-joy and-she-rejoiced in-spirit all her-inward-parts.
sentences.i: Then she saw holy Zion high up (?), shining like the sun; and when she saw her she gave thanks and praised the God of Israel, and bowed down, bent her neck, lifted her head, gazed into heaven, and thanked her Creator; she spread out her hands (?), cried out with her mouth (?), trod with her feet (?), and adorned all her body with joy, and she rejoiced in spirit with all her inward being (?).
sentences.n: A long chain of 3fs perfects, each joined by ወ-, as the Queen’s body takes part in worship. ርእየታ ‘she saw her’ (3fs perfect ርእየት + -ኣ ‘her’, giving -ታ); the object is restated as ለጽዮን ቅድስት ‘Zion the holy’, the Ark. በመልዕልት ‘on high, above’ (መልዕልት ‘height’; the exact sense is uncertain, ?). እንዘ ታበርህ ‘while she shines’ (causative of በርሀ, ‘be bright’); ከመ እንተ ፀሐይ ‘like that (f.) of the sun’. አእኰተቶ ‘she gave thanks to him’ and ሰብሐቶ ‘she praised him’ (3fs perfect + -ኦ ‘him’, giving -ቶ); ለአምላከ እስራኤል repeats the object, ‘God of Israel’. ሰገደት ‘bowed’, ጐድአት ‘she bent’, አልዐለት ‘she raised’ (causative of ዐለወ), ነጸረት ‘she looked’. The actions of the hands, mouth and feet (ጠፍሐት, የበበት, አጽሐሰት) are uncertain verbs, and I give the likeliest sense from context: clapping or spreading hands, ululation, stamping or dancing (?). አሰርገወት ‘she adorned’; ተሐሥየት ‘she was glad’ (tä-stem); ኵሉ ውሳጥያቲሃ ‘all her inward parts’ I take as the seat of her gladness, ‘in spirit, with all her inward parts’ (?). The scene recalls David dancing before the Ark (2 Samuel 6:14).

sentences.t: ወምንተ ፡ እብል ፡ ዘኮነ ፡ አሜሃ ፡ ፍሥሓ ፡ ለብሔረ ፡ ኢትዮጵያ ፡ እምሰብእ ፡ እስከ ፡ እንስሳ ፡ እምንኡስ ፡ እስከ ፡ ዐቢይ ፡ ወእምአንስት ፡ እስከ ፡ ተባዕት ።
sentences.l: And-what I-say which-was then joy to-land-of Ethiopia from-man until beast from-small until great and-from-women until males.
sentences.i: And what shall I say of the joy that was then in the land of Ethiopia, from man to beast, from small to great, from women to men?
sentences.n: The narrator speaks in the first person: ምንተ እብል ‘what shall I say?’ (ምንት ‘what’ accusative; እብል 1cs imperfect). ዘኮነ ‘which was’; አሜሃ ‘then’. ፍሥሓ ‘joy’. ለብሔረ ‘for the land of’ (construct). The pairs እምሰብእ እስከ እንስሳ ‘from man to beast’ and the like are a merism: everyone, even the animals. The same pairs appear in unit 11.

sentences.t: ወተከለት ፡ ደባትራ ፡ ወኀይመታተ ፡ መትሕተ ፡ ደብረ ፡ መክዳ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ስፉሕ ፡ ምድር ፡ ኀበ ፡ ሠናይ ፡ ማይ ፡ ወጠብሐት ፡ መጋዝአ ፡ ላህም ፡ ወአስዋረ ፡ መጠነ ፡ ፫፼ወ፳፻ ፡ ወአንበርዋ ፡ ለጽዮን ፡ ውስተ ፡ ሕጽነ ፡ ደብረ ፡ ማክዳ ፤
sentences.l: And-she-pitched tents and-shelters beneath mount-of Makeda in broad land where good water and-she-slaughtered gathering ox and-aswar measure 30,000-and-2,000 and-they-placed-her Zion in bosom-of mount-of Makeda;
sentences.i: She pitched tents and shelters at the foot of Mount Makeda, in a broad land where the water was good; she slaughtered a herd (?) of oxen and “aswar” (an unknown word, perhaps another kind of animal, ?), as many as 32,000; and they set Zion in the bosom of Mount Makeda;
sentences.n: ተከለት ‘she planted, pitched’ (perfect 3fs) with ደባትራ ‘tents, hangings’ and ኀይመታተ ‘tents’ (accusative plurals); መትሕተ ‘beneath’ (construct). ስፉሕ ምድር ‘broad land’ (adjective before noun). ኀበ ሠናይ ማይ ‘where (is) good water’. ጠብሐት ‘she slaughtered’; I take መጋዝአ ላህም as ‘a herd of oxen’ (?) and አስዋረ as another animal, a word unknown to me (?); the number, as many as 32,000, follows (መጠነ ‘as much as’). ፫፼ወ፳፻ is ፫፼ ‘three myriads’ (30,000) and ወ ‘and’ and ፳፻ ‘twenty hundred’ (2,000). አንበርዋ ‘they set her’ (perfect 3mp + -ዋ) with ለጽዮን restating her. ሕጽነ ‘bosom of’.

sentences.t: ወአግበረት ፡ ላቲ ፡ ዐቀብተ ፡ ፫፻ ፡ እኁዛነ ፡ አስይፍት ፡ ለጽዮን ፡ እለ ፡ የዐቅቡ ፡ ደባትሪሃ ፡ ለጽዮን ፡ ምስለ ፡ እሊአሃ ፡ ወመኳንንቲሃ ፡ ኀያላነ ፡ እስራኤል ፤
sentences.l: And-she-appointed for-her guards 300 holders-of swords for-Zion who they-guard tents-her to-Zion with her-peers and-her-nobles mighty-ones-of Israel;
sentences.i: She appointed for her three hundred guards, swordsmen, for Zion, who watch over Zion’s tents, together with her peers (?) and her nobles, the mighty men of Israel;
sentences.n: አግበረት ‘she made, appointed’ (causative of ገብረ), ላቲ ‘for her’ (Zion). ፫፻ is ‘three hundred’ (spoken ሠለስቱ ምእት). እኁዛነ ‘holders of’ (from አኀዘ ‘hold’, a participle in the plural), አስይፍት ‘swords’. እለ የዐቅቡ ‘who guard’ (እለ is the plural relative). ደባትሪሃ ‘her tents’ (-ሃ refers to Zion). ምስለ ‘with’; እሊአሃ is not clear to me: ‘her peers, companions’ (?). መኳንንቲሃ ‘her nobles’, ኀያላነ ‘the strong’. The ‘mighty men of Israel’ are the Israelite young men who accompanied Menelik (see the earlier chapters).

sentences.t: ወእሊአሃ ፡ ፫፻ ፡ እኁ ፡ ዛነ ፡ አስይፍት ፡ ወለወልዳሂ ፡ ንጉሥ ፡ ዳዊት ፡ ከማሆሙ ፡ ፯፻ ።
sentences.l: And-her-peers 300 holders swords and-for-her-son-too king David like-them 700.
sentences.i: Her peers (?) numbered three hundred swordsmen, and for her son, King David, likewise, seven hundred.
sentences.n: The source breaks እኁዛነ into እኁ ዛነ here, a word-division slip; read እኁዛነ. ለወልዳሂ ‘for her son too’ (ለ- + ወልድ + -ሃ + -ሂ ‘also’). ከማሆሙ ‘like them’. ፯፻ is ‘seven hundred’ (spoken ሰብዐቱ ምእት).

sentences.t: ወይትፌሥሑ ፡ ፈድፋደ ፡ በብዙኅ ፡ ክብር ፡ ወተድላ ፡ በሠናይ ፡ አልባስ ፤
sentences.l: And-they-rejoice exceedingly in-much glory and-delight in-good clothing;
sentences.i: They rejoiced exceedingly in great honour and delight, in fine clothing;
sentences.n: ይትፌሥሑ ‘they rejoice’ (imperfect, tä-stem), here a narrative present or continuing action. ፈድፋደ ‘exceedingly’ (adverb). በብዙኅ ክብር ‘in much glory’. አልባስ ‘clothing’.

sentences.t: እስመ ፡ አርትዐት ፡ መንግሥተ ፡ እምነ ፡ ባሕረ ፡ አሌባ ፡ እስከ ፡ ባሕረ ፡ ኣሴካ ፡ ወኵሉ ፡ ይትኤዘዝ ፡ በቃላ ፡ ወባቲ ፡ ክብረ ፡ ወብዕለ ፡ ፈድፋደ ፡ ዘአልቦ ፡ ዘኮነ ፡ እምቅድሜሃ ፡ ወኢይከውንሂ ፡ እምድኅሬሃ ።
sentences.l: For she-set-straight kingdom from sea-of Aleba until sea-of Aseka and-all he-obeys by-voice-her and-to-her glory and-wealth exceedingly which-not-is which-was before-her and-not-it-will-be-also after-her.
sentences.i: For she governed the kingdom rightly (?) from the Sea of Aleba to the Sea of Aseka (?), and all obeyed her voice; she had glory and wealth in great abundance, such as had not been before her and will not be after her.
sentences.n: እስመ ‘for’ gives the reason for the joy. አርትዐት ‘she set right, ruled justly’ (causative of ርትዐ, ‘be upright’), with መንግሥተ ‘the kingdom’ as object (?). እምነ ባሕረ ‘from the sea of’: ባሕረ is construct; አሌባ and ኣሴካ are unidentified and I keep them as written (?). ይትኤዘዝ ‘he obeys’ (tä-stem). ባቲ ‘in her is, she has’ (በ + -ቲ ‘her’, on the pattern of ቦ ‘there is to him’). ዘአልቦ ዘኮነ ‘which there is none that was’, i.e. ‘the like of which never was’. ኢይከውንሂ ‘nor will it be’ (-ሂ ‘also, even’: ‘nor even’).

sentences.t: እስመ ፡ በውእቱ ፡ መዋዕል ፡ በኢየሩሳሌም ፡ ሰሎሞን ፡ ንጉሥ ፡ ወበኢትዮጵያ ፡ መክዳ ፡ ንግሥት ፡ ለክልኤሆሙ ፡ ተውህበ ፡ ጥበብ ፡ ወክብር ፡ ወብዕል ፡ ወሞገስ ፡ ወአእምሮ ፡ ወሥነ ፡ ቃል ፡ ወልቡና ፤
sentences.l: For in those days in Jerusalem Solomon king and-in-Ethiopia Makeda queen to-both-of-them was-given wisdom and-glory and-wealth and-favour and-knowledge and-beauty-of word and-understanding;
sentences.i: For in those days Solomon was king in Jerusalem and Makeda was queen in Ethiopia, and to both of them were given wisdom, glory, wealth, favour, knowledge, eloquence, and understanding;
sentences.n: The nominal clauses በኢየሩሳሌም ሰሎሞን ንጉሥ ‘in Jerusalem, Solomon king’ and በኢትዮጵያ መክዳ ንግሥት need no verb. ለክልኤሆሙ ‘to the two of them’ (ክልኤቱ ‘two’ + -ሆሙ). ተውህበ ‘it was given’ (tä-stem of ወሀበ, singular, agreeing with the first noun). ሞገስ ‘favour, grace’; ሥነ ቃል ‘beauty of speech’ (ሥነ construct); ልቡና ‘understanding’. The author sets Solomon and Makeda side by side as equals, each with a kingdom, recalling the book’s theme of the two kingdoms, Jerusalem and Ethiopia.

sentences.t: ወወርቅ ፡ ወብሩር ፡ ኀስረ ፡ ከመ ፡ ብርት ፡ ወዲባጋት ፡ ዘወርቅ ፡ ኮነ ፡ ከመ ፡ ዐግያት ፡ ዘፈትል ፡ ወእንስሳ ፡ ወአፍራስ ፡ ዘአልቦ ፡ ኆልቈ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.l: And-gold and-silver diminished like [bərt] and-brocades of-gold were like cords of thread and-cattle and-horses which-not-with-it number.
sentences.i: Gold and silver were reduced to the worth of [bərt] (a metal; ?), and brocades of gold were like bands of thread (?), and cattle and horses were without number.
sentences.n: ኀስረ ‘it lacked, was lessened’ (perfect 3ms), here ‘was made worth little’ (?): gold and silver were so plentiful they were as cheap as ብርት, a metal word I cannot confirm (ch. 21–22 leaves it as [bərt], ?). ዲባጋት ዘወርቅ ‘brocades of gold’ (ዲባጋት, plural of a loan word for silk brocade; ዘ- ‘of’). ኮነ ከመ ‘was like’. ዐግያት ዘፈትል ‘bands of thread’ (?). እንስሳ ‘cattle, beasts’; አፍራስ ‘horses’. ዘአልቦ ኆልቈ ‘without number’, as in unit 14. The ፨ series ends the chapter.

sentences.t: ፹፮ ፡ ኀበ ፡ አንገሠቶ ፡ ማክዳ ፡ ለወልዳ ።
sentences.l: 86. Where made-king-him Makeda to-her-son
sentences.i: Chapter 86: Where Makeda Made Her Son King
sentences.n: Chapter heading. ኀበ ‘where’ (as in the title of ch. 85, ‘the place where’; ‘how’ would also suit). አንገሠቶ ‘she made him king’ (3fs perfect of the causative አንገሠ of ነግሠ, + -ኦ ‘him’, giving -ቶ), with ለወልዳ ‘her son’ repeating the object. Her son is the Menelik–David of the earlier chapters.

sentences.t: ወአመ ፡ ሣልስት ፡ ዕለት ፡ አወፈየቶ ፡ ለወልዳ ፡ አፍራሰ ፡ ኅሩያነ ፡ እለ ፡ የዐቅቡ ፡ ተዓይነ ፡ ፀር ፡ ወያመዘብሩ ፡ ካዕበ ፡ አህጉረ ፡ ፀር ፡ ፯፻ ፡ ወ፼ ፡ ወ፸፻ ፡ ወጋኝተ ፡ አፍራስ ፡ እለ ፡ ይወልዳ ፡ ፸ወ፯፻ ፡ ወበቅለ ፡ አንስት ፡ ፲፻ ፡ ወበቅለ ፡ ተባዕት ፡ ኅሩያነ ፡ ፯፻ ፡ ወአልባሰ ፡ ክብር ፡ ወርቀ ፡ ወብሩረ ፡ ስፉረ ፡ በጎሞር ፡ ወመጠነ ፡ መስፈርተ ፡ ቆሮስ ፡ በበ ፡ ሳድስ ፡ ወሳብዕ ፡ ወአወፈየቶ ፡ ኵሎ ፡ ዘበሕጉ ፡ ወመንበረ ፡ መንግሥታኒ ፤
sentences.l: And-on third day she-presented-him to-her-son horses chosen who they-guard watchers-of enemy and-they-ravage again cities-of enemy 700 and-10,000 and-7,000 and-mares-of horses who they-give-birth 70-and-700 and-mules-of females 1,000 and-mules-of males chosen 700 and-garments-of glory gold and-silver counted by-gomor and-as-much measure-of kor each sixth and-seventh and-she-presented-him all that-by-his-law and-throne-of kingdom-also;
sentences.i: On the third day she presented to her son chosen horses, such as watch out for enemy scouts (?) and moreover ravage the cities of the enemy, 17,700 of them; mares (?) that bear foals, 770; female mules, 1,000; chosen male mules, 700; garments of honour; gold and silver, counted out by the gomor, and by the measure of the kor, by sixths and sevenths (?); and she presented him with all that is by his law (?) and the throne of the kingdom as well;
sentences.n: A long list of gifts, in the accusative (አፍራሰ ‘horses’, ጋኝተ ‘mares’ (a guess from እለ ይወልዳ ‘which bear’, ?), በቅለ ‘mules’, ወርቀ ‘gold’, ብሩረ ‘silver’), all objects of አወፈየቶ ‘she presented him’ (causative of ወፈየ, ‘give gifts’). አመ ሣልስት ዕለት ‘on the third day’. እለ የዐቅቡ ተዓይነ ፀር ‘which keep (watch for) the ተዓይን of the enemy’, where ተዓይን may be ‘lookouts, scouts’ (?); ወያመዘብሩ ‘and which ravage’ (መዘበረ, causative, ‘plunder’). The numbers: ፯፻ ወ፼ ወ፸፻ is 700 + 10,000 + 7,000, i.e. 17,700; ፸ወ፯፻ is 770; ፲፻ is 1,000; ፯፻ is 700. ጎሞር is the omer or gomor (Exodus 16:36) and ቆሮስ the kor (a dry measure); በበ ሳድስ ወሳብዕ ‘by sixths and sevenths’ I cannot fit to a clear sense (?). ዘበሕጉ ‘what is by his law’ and ወመንበረ መንግሥታኒ ‘and the throne of the kingdom too’ (-ኒ ‘also’) are uncertain: perhaps the royal customs and regalia of the Queen’s realm (?).

sentences.t: ኵሎ ፡ አወፈየቶ ፡ ለወልዳ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.l: All she-presented-him to-her-son.
sentences.i: She gave all of it to her son.
sentences.n: ኵሎ ‘all’, accusative, placed first for emphasis; አወፈየቶ ‘she presented him’ with ለወልዳ ‘to her son’ for the receiver. The ፨ run closes chapter 86 and the part.
